dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise.
Hi Denise. Well, I'm not calling to tell you the tree fell on my head, so that's good news. Um, but there is a whole tree down across the street by me.
Okay, a whole tree. Is it blocking the road?

Yes, it's across a side street, side to side. Cars can't get through, they've been backing out since yesterday. It came down after the nor'easter, the one that ended Saturday. I figured it would get picked up, but it's Tuesday now and it's still sitting there.
Yeah, we've had a lot of those since the weekend. What's the address, or the closest one?
I'm at 403 Dixon Street, in the North End. The tree is on the little side street right next to my house, not on Dixon itself.
Got it, 403 Dixon. Can you tell if the tree is coming off private property or a city tree out by the curb?

That's sort of my question. I honestly can't tell. It looks like it came out of the yard of the house on the corner, but the roots are close to the sidewalk. So who do I call for this? Is it the city, the owner, or the utility? I'm not even sure where you report a downed tree.

You called the right place to report it, so that's done once I take it down. Generally, if it's a city street tree, we handle it. If it's from private property, the owner is responsible for removing it, though if it's blocking the road we'll often get it cleared enough to open the street. And the utility only comes into it if there are wires involved.
Wires. Hold on, let me look out the window. [pause] Okay, there's a cable line that's sagging, kind of draped over a branch. I don't know whose it is. It's not on the ground though.

Alright, don't go near it. I'll note that there's a line tangled in the branches. The utility would need to deal with that part, and our crew will want to know before they cut anything. Is anyone hurt, any cars or houses hit?
No, nothing hit. It just missed the neighbor's car by a few feet. Everybody's fine.
Good. Let me get the details down. Large tree, fully across the side street beside 403 Dixon, line caught in the branches, no damage or injuries. Did I get that right?
That's right. The street is a narrow one, so there's really no way around it.
Understood. Can I get a callback number in case the crew needs to reach you about access?

401-555-0169. Perfect. I'll put this in as a road blockage so it gets looked at ahead of the regular cleanup. Realistically, you're looking at sometime in the next day or two for the road to be opened. Whether the tree itself gets hauled away depends on who owns it.
Okay. And if it turns out to be the corner house's tree, do you tell them, or do I?

Our crew will check when they get out there, and if it's private, we'll go through the owner. You don't need to chase them down. If you happen to talk to them, though, it doesn't hurt to let them know.
Good, I'll mention it if I see them. And the cable company, do I call them about the sagging line?

You can, yes. Whoever's name is on your cable bill, call them and say there's a line down in a tree on Dixon Street. If it's an electric line instead, that's a different number, but it sounds like cable from what you describe.
Yeah, it's thin, so I think it's cable. I'll call them this afternoon. Then I'm done for the day. I plan to go to bed early tonight, so if somebody knocks, it won't be me answering.
No worries, crews don't usually knock anyway. They'll just work from the street. Anything else I can help with?
No, that's it. Thanks, Denise.
You're welcome. Take care, and stay clear of that line.
Will do. Bye now.
